newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch Computer Company plans share flotations.
newsitem.headline: Dutch Computer Company plans share flotations.

text.p: Dutch-based Computer Company said it had almost completed the procedure to be listed on the pan-European EASDAQ electronic exchange and was eying a flotation on a second bourse, possibly in Amsterdam.
It was looking at the possibility of a second listing with its financial advisor, Belgium's Generale Bank NV, the company said in a statement.

Computer Company said it would raise the number of its outstanding shares by 25 percent through the flotations. The proceeds would be used to strengthen its balance sheet ratios and finance further growth.
Expansion is seen taking place through opening new outlets, selective takeovers and investments in activities with high added value.

Computer Company is the parent of Computer Company Nederland BV and Computer Company Belgie NV. The firm, which started business in 1992, posted 1996 net profits of 9.6 million guilders on turnover of 311 million.
In 1995, the company generated net profits of six million guilders on turnover of 260 million. It has 400 employees, compared with 325 at the start of 1997 and 240 one year earlier.
Computer Company designs, installs and manages computer and telephone networks. It sells its products through six regional business centres in the Netherlands and two in Belgium.
In August, a seventh Dutch outlet will be opened and another will be expanded, the group said.
